title: DecolonialAuditRecord
description: v2. Extends the v1 schema in website-site-architecture.md by promoting the socio-technical dimension out of deconstructive_analysis into its own top-level, co-equal section (infrastructure_critique), and by structuring it so an information-systems reader can identify the exact class of technical mechanism being audited. See docs/audit-schema-guide.md for the design rationale and how to extend this.

record_id.description: Unique id, format SAGE-<AUTHOR3>-<YEAR>-P<PAGE>. If a page has more than one audited unit, append -A, -B, ... .

literal_excerpt.description: Verbatim quotation only. No paraphrase, no interpretation. This is the Wolcott (2009) transparency layer -- every downstream tag must be traceable back to this exact string.

deconstructive_analysis.description: Discipline 1: decolonial sociology (Santos, Grosfoguel, Trouillot). What the passage renders non-existent, and which historical epistemicide it re-enacts.

monoculture_tags.description: One or more of Santos's five monocultures. Use the short codes from decolonial-methods-audit-protocol.md Section 2.1.

erased_entity.description: Who or what knowledge-form is rendered ignorant/residual/inferior/local/unproductive by this passage.

rhetorical_device.description: The Fairclough-style CDA layer -- the lexical/rhetorical move that manufactures authority (e.g. efficiency metaphors, passive voice, 'rigor' as gatekeeping term).

framework.description: Citing REF ids from master-reference-key.md, e.g. '[REF-GRO-2013]; [REF-TRO-1995]'.

silence_moment.description: Trouillot's (1995) four moments of archival silencing.

infrastructure_critique.description: Discipline 2: information science / critical data studies (Olson, Patin et al., Trouillot-as-archival-theorist, Duarte & Belarde-Lewis, Berman, Sutherland). NEW in v2 -- see docs/audit-schema-guide.md '#1' for why this is its own top-level section rather than a nested field.

mechanism_type.description: The CLASS of infrastructure being audited, not the specific product. This is the taxonomy an IT/data-architecture reader will actually recognize from their own work. Closed vocabulary, extend deliberately (see guide).

named_system_or_practice.description: The specific tool or practice named or implied in the excerpt, e.g. 'ZyIndex', 'LEXIS/NEXIS', 'precoded protocol variables'.

technical_function.description: Plain, accurate description of what the mechanism actually does computationally/organizationally -- written so a systems person would recognize it as correct, not just rhetorically damning.

gatekeeping_effect.description: The direct consequence for what becomes findable/codable/legible, stated as an effect of the mechanism_type, not restated sociology.

is_it_literature.description: REF ids from master-reference-key.md Section 3 (Archival Power, Metadata, & Epistemicide in Information Studies). This array is what makes the 'second named discipline' claim falsifiable rather than asserted -- every infrastructure_critique should cite at least one.

reconstructive_ecology.description: The synthesis move: Santos's Ecologies answering the Monocultures tagged above, validated against qualitative-methods reliability standards.
